title: The cross-league Sleeper overlay stamps sleeperDataReady:true on a chimeric block — dynasty_new's real teams welded to dynasty_main's scoringSettings, rosterPositions and num_teams — which un-gates every team-dependent page
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md contract annotations: 'meta.sleeperDataReady — true iff sleeper block is valid for the *requested* league; false when the server served the shared rankings but doesn't have the requested league's rosters loaded' and 'meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey — which league the sleeper block *would* be for, when sleeperDataReady: false (diagnostic only)'.
observed: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, server.py:3244-3256 carries positions / playerIds / idToPlayer / scoringSettings / rosterPositions / leagueSettings forward from the LOADED league and lays the requested league's overlay (teams, trades, waivers) on top, then unconditionally sets meta.sleeperDataReady = True at :3259. GET /api/data?view=app&leagueKey=dynasty_new returns sleeperDataReady:true AND sleeperLoadedLeagueKey:"dynasty_main" simultaneously — a combination the documented contract says cannot occur. The block reports leagueId 1320092771247222784 and 10 real teams (correct) alongside num_teams 12, 58 roster slots and dynasty_main's 141-key IDP scoring card (all wrong; the real league is 10 teams, 27 slots, 48 keys, no IDP). useTeam.js:84-94 reads the flag: true -> leagueMismatch false -> the data-not-ready state that exists precisely for this case never renders.

reproduction.expected: sleeperDataReady:false (per the documented contract) OR a sleeper block whose scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings belong to dynasty_new
reproduction.actual: sleeperDataReady:true with num_teams 12, 58 roster slots, rec 0.08 and idp_sack 2.92 — dynasty_main's values under dynasty_new's leagueId and leagueName

userImpact: On /trade, /waivers and /rosters under dynasty_new the starter/bench split comes from sleeper.rosterPositions (frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:105), so the user is shown a 21-slot IDP lineup with 3 DL / 3 LB / 3 DB / 1 K starting slots for a league that has none of those positions, plus 37 bench slots for a 17-bench league — and the 'no roster data yet' banner that would have prevented all of it is suppressed.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A19-F20 and PRIOR-A21-F05 report the same class (hardcoded league context leaking across leagues) in ROS/public-league; this is the contract-level source those inherit from.

whatWorks: The no-overlay fallback path directly below (server.py:3288-3298) does it correctly: it nulls the sleeper block and sets sleeperDataReady:false. The defect is only on the overlay-succeeded branch.
rootCause: The overlay merge treats 'we fetched the requested league's rosters' as equivalent to 'the sleeper block is valid for the requested league', but the overlay only supplies teams/trades/waivers — scoringSettings, rosterPositions and leagueSettings are never overlaid and silently retain the loaded league's values.
requiredRepair: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, either drop scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings from the carried-forward key list (leaving them absent rather than wrong) and keep sleeperDataReady:false, or fetch the requested league's own config in the overlay so the block is genuinely that league's. Do not stamp sleeperDataReady:true unless every field in the block belongs to the requested league.
dependencies: W18-F001 — with a correct scoringProfile this path would 503 before reaching the overlay.

b6Resolution.resolution: The cross-league sleeper merge was inline in four request handlers, which is why no test covered it. It is now one named function, src/api/sleeper_overlay.py::merge_cross_league_sleeper_block, with the invariant 'sleeperDataReady is true IFF every league-specific field represented as ready belongs to the requested league'. scoringSettings / rosterPositions / leagueSettings come from the requested league's own config or are left ABSENT; the NFL-wide maps (positions, playerIds, idToPlayer) are genuinely league-independent and still reused.
b6Resolution.howReadyStaysReachable: fetch_sleeper_overlay now publishes leagueConfig, read from the same Sleeper league object _fetch_league_name already fetched — no extra round-trip. A cross-league block that owns its config is still ready, so the repair does not cost working functionality; only an unfetchable config degrades to not-ready.
b6Resolution.independenceNote: The regression fixture is deliberately NOT the real dynasty_main -> dynasty_new pair. That pair was only reachable because W18-F001 let two differently-scored leagues share a label; after the F001 repair it correctly 503s before the overlay runs, so a test built on it would have evaporated. League A and B in the fixture are genuinely scoring-compatible and differ only in league-specific configuration. Verified still RED for its own reason (no named merge function) after F001 went green.

ownerReviewGaps.completeConfigRequired: ready=True previously needed only a truthy scoringSettings, so a partial Sleeper response (valid scoring, rosterPositions [], leagueSettings {}) published as ready. league_config_is_complete() now decides, traced to the consumers: rosterPositions must be NON-EMPTY (bdvm/league_config.py gates on `if roster_positions and scoring:` so [] falls through to the registry, and frontend/lib/starter-slots.js ranks the live list above the registry, so an empty live list yields an empty lineup), and leagueSettings must carry num_teams > 1 (the same builder raises LeagueConfigError at teams <= 1). No empty-but-present value is legitimately complete. _fetch_league_config returns None on a partial answer instead of passing skeletons downstream.
